entries.title: Kitchen: cook with the real cooking model
items: Kitchen row north of the spawn: 4 ingredient crates, board, pan, pot, counter
Names and star ratings come from the server's cooking simulation
Labels above food update live for every player
test: Potato crate (E), board 3 (sticks), pan 2 (golden): 'crispy fried potato sticks' with 4 stars
Pan 3 (dark) gives fewer stars than pan 2
Both players cook at the same time

entries.title: Money: buy, cook, sell
items: Everyone starts with $500; crates charge the grocer price
The counter plates and sells to NPC demand; better cooking pays more
One in-game hour per minute: demand refills, prices move
test: Golden fries sell for more than dark fries
A raw potato cannot be sold
Sell many of the same dish: the price drops, the next hour demand returns

entries.title: Controls: third-person camera, sprint, sneak, jump
items: Mouse turns the camera (cursor locked); Esc or Alt frees the cursor
WASD moves where the camera looks; Shift sprints, C sneaks, Space jumps
Your own movement is predicted, so it feels instant even with lag
test: Camera does not go through boxes or stations
Jump while carrying something: no bump at the top
Gamepad: sticks move and look, A/cross jumps, B/circle sneaks

entries.title: New HUD, F1 debug menu, this banner
items: Clean HUD: wallet, time of day, what you hold, station hints, sales toasts
All technical details moved to the debug menu: press F1
This banner shows what is new in each build; F2 opens it again
test: F1 toggles the debug menu, F2 reopens this banner, Enter closes it
Near a station the hint at the bottom shows its keys
Selling a dish shows a toast on the right

entries.title: Talk without voice: emotes, pings, quick chat
items: Hold G (gamepad LB), move the mouse to an emote, release: it shows above your head
Middle mouse (gamepad RB) pings where you look; double-click marks danger
Hold T and press 1-6 for quick chat lines (gamepad D-pad)
test: The other window sees your emote bubble and the ping pillar
Quick chat appears as a toast for nearby players
Spamming G or middle mouse gets limited after a few tries

entries.title: Meals: plating table and mixing bowl
items: Plating table and bowl next to the counter (end of the kitchen row)
E with food in hand puts it on the plate / in the bowl; E with empty hands takes the result
A plate with two or more things is a meal: it sells for about 3x a single snack
test: Golden fries + tomato slices on one plate, take it, sell it: about $1,400
Two players fill the same plate together
A finished plate cannot go onto another plate

entries.title: Customers: the town's demand walks in
items: NPC customers walk in from the east and queue at the counter with their wish above the head
Orange wants a meal, green a snack, blue a drink
Sell a dish: one customer takes it and leaves with 'Thanks!'; unserved ones leave at the next hour
test: At 08:00 a queue forms in front of the counter
Sell a meal: an orange customer leaves happy
Wait an in-game hour (1 minute): the queue changes

entries.title: Cooking takes time: switch on the pan and the pot
items: Pan and pot cook over time: E puts food in, E with empty hands takes it out
1 switches the pan or pot on and off; food only cooks while it is on (they start off)
The label shows what is inside and how far: raw, warming up, short, medium, long
Pan: 2 switches fry or saute (only while the pan is empty)
test: Potato sticks in the pan, press 1 (on), take out after about 25 s: 'crispy fried potato sticks'
Switch off with food inside: the label stops changing; switch on again and it goes on
Take food out right away: 'Too short', it comes back unchanged
A puts food in the pan, B takes it out: works for both players

entries.title: The kitchen and the street get real art
items: Kitchen stations are now stoves, cabinets and a bar instead of grey boxes (free CC0 models)
A short street east of the kitchen with a road, houses, a shop, street lights and trees
Movement, interaction range and cooking are unchanged
test: Walk along the kitchen row: every station shows a model and its label is readable
Walk to the counter: customers queue on the street side next to the road
Cook one dish end to end: it works as before

entries.title: Food you can see
items: Food is a 3D model now: potatoes, apples, tomatoes and onions look like themselves
Cut food shows its shape (halves, slices, sticks, cubes); fried potato sticks become fries
Cooked food gets darker the longer it cooks; fried food turns golden
Plates and bowls show what is on them, the pan and the pot show what is cooking
test: Take a potato from the crate: it looks like a potato (a brown oval) in your hands
Board 3 (sticks): it turns into sticks; board 2 on a tomato gives tomato slices
Fry the sticks for about 25 s: they come out as golden fries, darker than raw sticks
Put fries and tomato slices on the plating table: both show on the plate, also after taking it
Put food in the pan and switch it on: the other player sees it in the pan and it darkens

entries.title: First-person view
items: You now see the town through your own eyes; V (or pressing the right stick) switches to the camera behind you and back
A small dot in the middle of the screen shows what you look at; E and 1-4 act on that station or food
The food you carry is shown in the lower right of your view
In first person your character faces where you look, so you can walk sideways and backwards
The game remembers the view you used last
test: Start the game: you look from your eyes and see a dot in the middle of the screen
Look at the board from close by: the dot lights up and the board's keys show under it
Look at the potato crate and press E: you hold a potato in the lower right of your view
Look at a wall or the floor and press E: you drop the potato
Press V: the camera moves behind you and looks the same way; press V again to go back
Ask another player: in first person your body turns to where you look

entries.title: Cut with the knife, stoves with buttons
items: First person needs no number keys any more: you cook with E and the mouse
The board has a cutting board and a knife next to it; the knife is an item you can carry and put down
Put food on the board, take the knife, hold the left mouse button and drag down to cut; right click turns the food
One cut gives halves, two give slices; turn and cut for sticks, turn and cut again for cubes
The pan and the pot have a switch (green when on); the pan also has a fry/sauté button
Third person keeps the old number keys
test: Hold a potato, look at the board and press E: the potato lies on the cutting board
Look at the knife next to it and press E: you hold the knife in your view
Look at the board, hold the left button and drag down twice: the knife chops and the potato becomes slices
Right click, drag down once more: sticks; right click and cut again: cubes
Put the knife down (look at the floor, E), then take the food from the board with E
Look at the pan's switch and press E: it turns green; the button next to it switches fry and sauté
Ask another player: they see the potato fall apart and the switch light change

entries.title: Use the kitchen with the mouse
items: First person: left click does what the text under the dot says; E is gone, Q drops what you hold
What you look at lights up: white = take, green = put or use, grey = not possible (the text says why)
Worktops between the stations: click with something in your hands to put it down on the green spot
The knife now has its own spot next to the cutting board; put it on any worktop and take it back
Station labels are smaller in first person and fade out when you stand right at them
Third person keeps E and the number keys
test: Look at the potato crate with empty hands: it glows white, 'Click · take potato ($60)'; click
Look at the pot: it glows green, 'Click · put potato into the pot'. Look at the board instead and click
Look at the knife and click to pick it up; hold the left button and drag down on the potato to cut
With the knife, look at a worktop: a green spot shows where it goes; click, then click the knife again to take it
Hold a finished plate over the pan: grey 'can't go in there', the click does nothing
Press Q to drop what you hold; ask another player whether they see your knife on the worktop

entries.title: Cookware you can carry: pans, pots, plates, the board and the bowl
items: The kitchen is worktops, two stoves with two burners each, the counter and a plate shelf
The cutting board, pan, pot, bowl and plates lie on top and can be picked up and put anywhere
Put a pan or pot on a burner and switch that burner on with its knob; it only cooks while it stands there
A pot takes up to four ingredients; each one cooks for its own time, and they are mixed when you pour
Holding a pan, pot or bowl with food, click a plate (or a bowl) to pour it in; sell the plate at the counter
Take clean plates from the shelf (at most 8 in the kitchen); lost cookware comes back to its spot
test: With empty hands click the pan: you pick it up. Click the free burner on the other stove: the pan stands there
Buy a potato and click the stove top behind the pan: the potato lies there next to it
Buy a potato, cut it on the board, click the pot: it goes in. Buy an onion and put it in the pot too
Click the knob under the pot's burner: it lights green and the burner ring glows; the label shows both ingredients cooking
After a while pick up the pot (empty hands), click a plate: the pot's mix lies on the plate
Pick up the plate and click the counter: it sells with stars and the plate is gone
Ask another player: they see the pan move, the pot's contents and the plate in your hands

entries.title: Customer orders and a short shift
items: Every customer orders a dish from the menu: Fries, Potato soup, Onion soup, Tomato salad, Fried apple, Veggie mix
The order floats above the customer and hangs as a card on the ticket rail above the counter, with the minutes waited
Sell a plate at the counter: the first customer whose order it matches gets it, else the first in line
Exact order: full price plus 10 % tip per star above 2. Close (one step off): 60 %. Wrong dish: 25 %
A shift runs from 08:00 to 14:00 in-game (6 minutes). Then everyone sees the summary for 15 s and the next day starts at 08:00
F3 shows the shift summary (served, earned, average stars, missed); the top left shows open orders
test: Fries: potato, cut into sticks (3 strokes with a turn), into the pan on a burner that is on, about 25 s, pour onto a plate, sell: a fries customer says 'Thanks!'
Potato soup: potato cut in halves, into the pot on a burner, about 1 minute, pour onto a plate
Onion soup: an onion and one more ingredient into the pot together, about 1 minute, pour onto a plate
Tomato salad: tomato slices and a cut onion into the bowl, pour the bowl onto a plate (no heat)
Fried apple: switch the burner to saute with its mode button first, apple slices or halves into the pan, a few seconds
Veggie mix: three different cut ingredients on one plate
Serve a wrong dish on purpose: the customer leaves red, 'That's not what I ordered', and pays little
Play until 14:00: the queue leaves, the summary shows your numbers for 15 s, then a new shift starts at 08:00

entries.title: Kitchen polish: sounds, steam and real counters
items: Chopping on the board makes a knife sound; picking up, putting down and the stove knobs tick softly
A pan on a burner that is on sizzles, a pot bubbles (the sounds are generated in code, nothing is downloaded)
Pans and pots with food on a hot burner give off steam
The worktops are kitchen cabinets now instead of grey boxes
The prompt under the dot sits on a dark rounded panel with white text, so it reads over the highlight
test: Cut a potato on the board: every stroke chops
Put the pan with food on a burner and switch it on: it sizzles and steams, switch it off and both fade
Do the same with the pot: it bubbles
Walk away from the stove: the sounds get quieter, nothing is too loud
Aim at a worktop and at something out of reach: the prompt is readable, the grey reason stays grey

entries.title: People instead of capsules
items: Players and customers are low-poly people (Kenney Mini Characters) with idle, walk, run and crouch animations
What you carry is in your right hand for everyone else (and for you in third person), not above your head
Customers are four different people, lightly tinted by what they want
First person is unchanged: you see your shadow and the item in view, not your own body
test: Two players: walk, sprint and crouch in front of each other; the other one walks, runs and crouches
Pick up a potato, a plate and the pan: the other player sees it in your hand, nothing floats
Third person (V): your own person holds the item; first person: the item is in view as before
Customers at the counter are people, the order text is still above their heads
Send an emote (G): the bubble is above the head and the person wobbles

entries.title: New people, calmer steps
items: Players and customers are new people at a real height of 1.75 m, with new animations: walking blends smoothly into running, sneaking has its own walk
Calmer movement: walking 2.5 m/s, sprinting 5 m/s, sneaking 1.25 m/s, and a lower jump
Shorter, quicker steps that match how fast you move, so feet no longer slide over the ground
Carried items sit in the right hand, with the forearm held forward
Customers are tinted in warm, soft colours by what they want
test: Two players: walk and sprint in front of each other; the feet stay on the ground and do not slide
Start and stop walking: it feels as quick as before, only slower
Jump: about half as high as before
Pick up a plate: the other player sees it in your right hand
First person (V) looks the same as before: your shadow and the item in view

entries.title: Real sizes, one set of colours
items: Everything is built at real size next to a 1.75 m person: houses about 7.5 m to the ridge, trees 4 and 8 m, street lamps 4.5 m
Worktops and stove tops are at 0.90 m, the serving counter at 1.05 m; worktops are rows of 60 cm cabinets
Food and cookware are smaller and fit together: an apple is 12 cm, the pan 52 cm, the pot 35 cm
One warm, soft colour palette for the kitchen, the street, the labels and the menus
The street is spaced for the bigger houses; one house now stands south of the road
test: Walk along the kitchen in third person: the tops are at hip height, nothing floats above or sinks into them
First person: pick up the pan and the pot; cook something and look into them: the food is inside, not on the rim
Put plates and the board on the worktops: they lie flat on the top
Walk down the street: houses, trees and lamps look the right size next to you and do not overlap
Open the HUD, the F1 menu and the What's-new banner: warm muted colours, everything readable

entries.title: The kitchen is a real street-food shop
items: A back line along a back wall: crates, prep worktop with the board, two stoves, plates, in the order you cook
A cook aisle in front of it, and a front counter between you and the guests; you serve across it
Guests queue along the counter's street side and face you; they never walk into the kitchen
Stove knobs, crates and labels all face the aisle; the order rail hangs above the counter, readable from the aisle
You start in the aisle; the staff gap at the left end leads out to the town
test: Spawn: you stand in the aisle facing the stoves; turn around and the guests wait across the counter
Cook fries and serve them at the counter without leaving the aisle
Walk out through the staff gap, around to the street, and look across the counter into the kitchen
Two players in the aisle: try to pass each other (it is 1.3 m wide) and say if it feels too tight

entries.title: Feel pass 1: instant answers, nothing teleports, forgiving aim
items: A click answers at once: the pan arcs into your hand, things settle onto the spot, food drops into the pot, each with its own sound
If the server says no, the item flies back with a short 'nope'
Everyone sees the arcs and drops, not only you
Aim takes the best target near the dot (a pot for the potato in your hand) and does not flicker between two
Outline and prompt on the target, grey 'Too far' when out of reach, and a see-through copy where the item will land
Fast double clicks are no longer lost; the third-person camera sits closer and lower
F2 opens the feel panel (development builds): sliders, Preset A and B, Save writes feel.json; the What's-new banner is Shift+F2 there
test: Pick up the pan, put it on a burner, drop a potato into the pot: does anything jump or wait for the server?
Aim at the free spot right next to the pan with a potato in hand: you get the spot, not the pan
Press F2, try Preset A and Preset B for a few minutes each and say which one feels better (A or B)
Third person (V): is the cook readable and the kitchen still visible?
Watch the other player stand and turn at the stove: legs together, no frozen stride

entries.title: Feel pass 2: cooking reads at a glance
items: A small ring next to a pan or pot on the heat fills up; the green and yellow rim marks the good window (yellow is perfect)
The food changes colour as it cooks: raw, golden, brown, and charcoal when it burns, also in the pot
The sizzle and bubbling grow with the heat and get a little higher when the food is overdone
A chime at perfect, three beeps 3 s before it overcooks, a hiss and dark smoke when it burns
Serving at the counter: stars pop over it, a coin sounds and the money and tip float up, for everyone near the counter
test: Fry a whole potato and watch the ring and the colour: can you take it out at perfect without reading any label?
Leave it on: do the beeps come early enough, and do the smoke and hiss read as burnt?
Serve a dish while the other player watches from the street: do both of you see the stars and the money?
First person: does the ring ever get in the way when you look at the pan?

entries.title: Readable world text and a varied crowd
items: Station and crate names are small signs on the front, readable from the cook side only, never through walls or mirrored
Order bubbles above guests no longer overlap: the first two in the queue show the full order, the others a letter
Item names and stars show only for the item you aim at or carry; nothing floats across the middle of the first-person view
Guests come in six looks (shirt, trousers and hair colours), each guest keeps its look
test: Stand in the street and look at the queue: can you read the first guest's order, and is nothing overlapping?
First person at a stove: is there any big text across the view?
Walk behind the counter and stove row: do the signs face you and stay clear of the knobs?
Do neighbouring guests in the queue look different?

entries.title: Street-food stock: ten new ingredients
items: A bank of ten narrow crates at the left end of the back line: flatbread, wrap, seitan, falafel mix, lettuce, cucumber, red cabbage, lemon, garlic-herb sauce, chili sauce
Each is bought, carried, placed and cut like the old four; prices $45 to $110 per item
A new test keeps every item, menu dish and patch note plant-based
The kitchen is wider: the staff gap is at the left end of the new bank
test: Walk to the left end of the kitchen: are the ten crates readable from the aisle?
Take a cucumber, put it on the board with the knife: two strokes give slices
Take a lemon and cut it: do you get halves, then slices?

entries.title: Compact stock: a fridge and a dry shelf next to the board
items: The crates are gone: every ingredient now stands in a fridge (vegetables, seitan, falafel mix, lemon, apple) or on a dry shelf (sauces, potato, onion, flatbread, wraps)
Both stand right next to the cutting board, so a dish needs only a few steps
Aim at an item in first person: it lights up and the prompt names it with its price; a click takes one and it flies into your hand
The kitchen is shorter again; the staff gap moved with it
test: First person at the fridge: does aiming pick the item you look at, and does the prompt show the right name and price?
Take a cucumber from the fridge and a potato from the shelf: do they fly into your hand without a jump?
With something in your hands, or without money, a take is refused: does the item fly back with a short sound?
Cook a full dish: are the fridge, the shelf and the board a few steps apart?

entries.title: Deep fryer: fries and falafel
items: A fryer with two baskets stands between the board and the stoves: switch it on with the middle knob
Put potato sticks or a falafel mix portion into a raised basket, press its button: the basket swings into the oil and bubbles
Watch the ring and listen: good at about 25 s, perfect at 30 s, burnt at 45 s (falafel 20, 25 and 38 s)
Click the basket in the oil once while it is good to shake it: an even fry is worth more
Press the button again: the basket lifts and drips for 2 s; take the food out before that and it is greasy
Fries go on a plate in their box; the menu now has Falafel (4)
test: Cut a potato into sticks, fry them and serve them to a customer who ordered Fries: does it feel quick and clear?
Do the basket arc, the bubbles and the sounds tell you when to shake and when to lift without looking at a timer?
Lift a basket and take the fries at once: does the prompt warn you that it is still dripping?
Is the fryer close enough to the board and the plates?

entries.title: Kitchen polish: labels, tipping fries, fryer touches
items: Food on the heat says what it looks like: pale, golden or dark fries; raw, warm, cooked, well done or burnt in a pan or pot
Hold a plate and click a raised basket: the fries tip onto the plate in their box
The fryer hums quietly while it is on with both baskets up; the drain drops are bigger
The stoves stand side by side, so the plates are a few steps from the fryer
Two cooks pressing the same basket button no longer cancel each other
Re-frying fries and shaking again no longer stacks the even-fry bonus
test: Fry fries: does the basket's label go from pale to golden to dark as the fries look?
Fetch a plate, hold it and click the raised basket: do the fries land on the plate?
Is the walk from the fryer to the plates and the counter short enough now?
Click a knife and right away a fridge slot: does nothing swap in your hand?

entries.title: The griddle: grill, flip, toast
items: A griddle with six spots stands between the prep board and the fryer; switch it on with the knob on its front
Each side of the food cooks on its own: the ring has a half per side, and only the side that is down fills
Pick up the spatula from the griddle's deck and click the food to flip it; grill marks show on the cooked side
New in stock: paprika, eggplant and mushroom on the dry shelf; bread toasts on the griddle in a few seconds
On the menu: Grilled veggies (grilled paprika and one more grilled vegetable on a plate) and Toasted flatbread
Labels on food that cooks now always show the name it gets when you take it out
test: Grill seitan strips: does the first half of the ring fill, and the second half after the flip?
Flip with the spatula: does the food turn over at once with a tssh, and do the grill marks show on top?
Right click the food without the spatula: does it say Use the spatula?
Hold a plate and click grilled food: does it slide onto the plate? Serve Grilled veggies to a guest
Is the griddle close enough to the board, the fryer and the plates?

entries.title: The assembly board: wraps, flatbreads and boxes
items: An assembly board stands after the plates, by the plate shelf: put a wrap or flatbread on it, then the fillings, the salad and the sauce
Every layer drops onto the stack; the order counts a little, missing parts count more, extra parts do not count
Hold left click on a sauce dispenser to squeeze: about half a second to one and a half seconds is the right amount
Click the build with empty hands to fold it, then click the wrap paper on the rack; a box or a bag comes from the rack too
On the menu: Seitan wrap, Falafel wrap, Seitan flatbread (folded, in a bag) and Veggie box (fries, grilled vegetables and sauce in a box)
test: Build a falafel wrap: wrap, falafel, lettuce slices, garlic-herb sauce. Does each layer land on the stack with a plop?
Hold the garlic-herb dispenser: does the bottle tip over the build with a ribbon and a squeeze sound while you hold?
Fold it, then wrap it in paper: are both short and clear? Serve it to a guest who ordered a Falafel wrap
Try paper before folding: does it say Fold it first, with nothing charged?
Is the board close enough to the plates and the counter?

entries.title: Kitchen polish: a calmer view, fair sauce prices, food you can see
items: Heat rings show only for what you aim at and for food about to overcook or burnt; in third person also the 4 nearest
The warning before overdone now fits short cooks: toast no longer warns before it is done
A squeeze of sauce costs a portion: 10% of the bottle per started half second, at most 30%; paper, box and bag keep their price
Food you hold stands whole in the lower right of your view; big things are drawn smaller so the middle stays free
The takeaway box is closed; a build without a dish name has a short label (wrap with golden...)
Grilled food keeps its grill marks on a plate; the spatula flips in your hand
Hold E (or the right trigger) at the board in third person, or the right trigger in first person, to squeeze
test: Fill all six griddle spots: in first person, do you see only the ring you aim at (plus warnings)?
Squeeze a short dash and a long squeeze: does the money go down by a small portion, not the whole bottle?
Hold a wrap: is it fully visible in the lower right? Hold a pan: does it stay out of the middle?
Box a build: does the box look closed?
Grill seitan strips and slide them onto a plate: do the grill marks stay?

entries.title: Orders 2.0: guests with wishes, patience, the register, tips and reviews
items: Guests say their order with changes in plain words: 'Falafel wrap, extra garlic' or 'no lettuce' (at most two)
The ticket rail shows them too: '+ extra garlic', and 'no lettuce' with a line through it
A ring over each waiting guest drains and turns red near the end; when it runs out the guest leaves
Hand the food over at the counter: the guest takes it, thanks you and waits at the register (no more waiting time there)
Card: click the terminal. Cash: the guest hands notes; click coins and notes into the tray for the change, then GIVE
Wrong change costs the difference and a star in the review; the tip (up to 30%) is for speed, the right order and quality
The shift summary (F3) adds tips, reviews with a short line and missed guests by reason
Third person: E at the assembly board squeezes only after a short hold; a tap still picks up and drops
test: Serve a guest who asked for 'extra garlic': squeeze long (lots). Is it an exact order?
Read the rail: is 'no lettuce' clearly struck through?
Let a guest wait: does its ring drain and turn red, and does it leave?
Take a cash payment: count out the change. Then give one coin too many next time: do you lose it and get a worse review?
Take a card payment with one click: does it beep?
Open the summary (F3): do you see tips, reviews and the missed guests?

entries.title: Drinks: cups, the dispenser and a fill line
items: A drink dispenser on the front counter, left of the serving counter: lemonade, iced tea and soda
Click the cup stack for a cup, then hold left click on a tap: the cup goes under it and fills while you hold
Stop at the line on the cup (about 1.8 s). Too little is half-full, over the brim it spills on the counter
Click the lid stack to put a lid on; a drink is sold with its lid on
About half the guests order a drink with their food ('+ lemonade' in the bubble and on the rail); hand over both, in any order, then they pay for both at once
A cup and its drink are charged once, when you let go of the tap; a top-up of the same drink pays no second cup
Third person: tap E at the dispenser for a cup or a lid, hold E to pour from the nearest tap
test: Fill a lemonade to the line: does the level rise from the moment you press, and stop where you let go?
Hold too long: does it splash and leave a puddle? Is the drink worth less?
Put a lid on an empty cup: is it refused? Lid a filled one: does it click?
Serve a wrap to a guest who wants a lemonade: does it wait for the drink, then go to the register with one bill?
Watch your money: is a pour charged once, cup plus drink, when you let go?

entries.title: Stock and supply: slots run empty, order at the terminal, unpack the delivery
items: Every fridge and shelf slot, the packaging rack, the cup stack and the drink taps now hold a counted stock; a new game starts at half
Taking from a slot is free (the order paid for it); the samples and the tag show what is left, an empty slot says 'empty'
Sauces come in bottles (a squeeze uses 10 to 30 % of one, the next opens from the dry shelf); drinks come in kegs of 20 cups
The ordering terminal hangs on the back wall by the staff door: pick a row (page and pack count with its buttons); it shows the price and the delivery time
Orders cost the supplier's bulk price (80 % of the grocer's) and are paid when you place them
About a minute later (one game hour) the boxes arrive on the worktop by the back door, with a knock
Carry a box (both hands) to its slot and click: the slot fills up to its capacity, the rest stays in the box
The HUD lists 'Low stock' under a quarter; third person: E unpacks into the station you stand at, E at the terminal orders the nearest row
test: Take tomatoes until the slot is empty: do the samples go one by one, does the tag turn red and say 'empty'?
Order one pack at the terminal: is the price taken from your money once, and does the feed say when it is due?
Wait for the knock: are the boxes on the worktop by the back door? Carry one: is it held low in front of you?
Unpack into the slot: does it fill at once, and a full slot keep the rest in the box?
Use up the cups or a sauce: is it refused with 'Out of stock'? Does the HUD say 'Low stock' first?

entries.title: Cleaning: dirty dishes, the sink, the trash, spills and the hygiene score
items: The shop owns eight plates. Half the guests eat in ('for here' on their bubble): their plate comes back dirty to the dish return on the counter, by the register, after their meal
Take a dirty plate from the dish return, put it in the sink next to the plate shelf, and hold to scrub (1.5 s): it goes back on the clean shelf. Without washing, plates run out
Throw burnt food, scraps and empty cups into the trash can by the staff gap; at 12 items it is full
With empty hands take the bag out of the can and carry it to the bin outside the staff gap
A spilled drink leaves a puddle: take the cloth from the sink's drainboard and hold it on the puddle to wipe it
The HUD shows the hygiene score (a drop and %): dirty dishes left out over two game minutes, a full trash, spills and burning food lower it; it recovers when all is clean
Guests notice: below 50 % a review loses a star, below 30 % new guests are 20 % less patient
test: Serve an eat-in guest a plate dish: about 20 s later, is a dirty plate on the dish return? Wash it: is the shelf one plate fuller?
Hold the scrub only a second: does the plate stay dirty? Hold it 1.5 s: is it clean, with bubbles and the scrub sound?
Fill the trash to 12: does it refuse more and turn red? Take the bag out to the bin: is it empty again?
Overfill a cup, then wipe the puddle with the cloth: does it shrink away?
Leave dishes and a spill: does the hygiene meter drop and turn yellow, then red? Clean up: does it climb again?

entries.title: The seitan spit: a turning cone, shaved with the knife
items: A seitan spit stands on the front counter, across the aisle from the stoves: a cone of seitan turns in front of a heat panel
Empty hands at the bare spit load a cone from stock (one cone is about 30 portions; order more at the terminal, a cone comes in its own box)
The knob turns the heat off, low or high. Only the outside cooks: it browns (the ring shows it), good at 40 s, perfect at 55 s, burnt at 90 s on high
Hold the knife on the cone to shave: one second is one portion. The curls fall into the catch tray (it holds 3), and the next layer starts half-way
Take a portion from the tray, or scoop it straight onto the wrap in your hands. Seitan wraps and flatbreads take shaved seitan or grilled strips, and the review says which
Hygiene now changes ten times slower (a spill costs 0.2 % a game minute)
test: Load a cone and switch the knob to high: does the cone turn and brown, the panel glow, the sizzle and the motor hum play?
Shave at about 55 s with the knife: do curls fall into the tray and the knife saw in your view? Is the tray at 1 after a 1 s hold, 3 after a long one?
Shave right after a shave: is the new seitan pale? Leave it on high for 90 s: does it char and smoke?
Build a seitan wrap with shaved seitan (scoop onto the wrap in your hands or put it on the board), wrap it and serve: does the review mention the spit?
Make a spill and watch the hygiene meter: does it fall slowly now (about 1 % every 5 s)?

entries.title: Your first shift: a guided tutorial through every station
items: A small card at the top shows one step at a time (3 / 14): take a potato, cut sticks, fry, plate, build and wrap a falafel wrap, serve, take the payment, lemonade, wash a plate, order stock, and the spit (optional)
The thing to use next pulses in mustard, even when you do not aim at it; an arrow at the screen edge points to it when it is out of view
A step you already did completes at once. F4 (or Skip tutorial) ends it, F5 skips the optional spit step; it starts by itself only on your first game
Play it again with Play the tutorial here or Replay tutorial in the F1 menu

When you host, the guests of your tutorial are calm (three times the patience) and the first ones order fries and a falafel wrap with lemonade, paid in cash. A dedicated server never changes its rules
Seitan cones can be ordered at the terminal again (they were priced as an unknown good)
test: Host a new game: does the card appear at the top, and does each step finish as soon as you do it?
Turn away from the shelf: does the edge arrow point the right way, and does the target pulse in mustard?
Hold a potato before step 2 shows: does step 2 finish at once?
Do the guests wait longer during the tutorial, and is the first guest's order fries (cash, eat in)?
Press F4: is the card gone, and does it stay gone after a restart? Replay it from F1 or Play the tutorial

entries.title: Put things down anywhere on the counters
items: Every counter top takes items now: both front counter runs (the cook side, also right beside the register, the dish return and the drink dispenser), the front strip of the stoves, the fryer's deck behind the oil, the back of the assembly board, the sink's front and back, and the plate shelf (its plate stack moved to the back left corner)

Only parts with a job of their own still refuse: burners take one pan each, the fryer baskets, the griddle spots, the sink basin, the spit, the build spot, the dispenser taps, the register, the serving counter and the trash can
You walk through food and things lying on the floor instead of climbing them like stairs
Knives, spatulas and the cloth lie with the handle towards you: at home the handle points into the aisle, and when you put one down it turns towards where you stand
test: Put a plate, a pan and the knife on the front counter left and right of the register and the drink dispenser, on the fryer deck and on the plate shelf: does it land where the green ghost was, at the right height, and can you pick it up again?
Aim at the guest half of the front counter with something in your hands: does the ghost show on the cook side?
Drop a tomato and walk over it: do you stay on the floor?
Put the knife down on the front counter and on a back worktop: does the handle point at you?
Does anything still refuse without a reason?

entries.title: Mouse-first controls: left click does, right click puts down
items: Left click does the obvious thing with what you aim at: pick up, take, press, put into the pot, slide onto the plate, cut, flip, serve. Hold left click to squeeze, pour, scrub, shave and wipe, as before

Right click always puts down what you hold: on the counter spot you aim at (the green ghost shows where; aiming at a pot or pan puts it next to it), or at your feet when you aim at no counter. It never does anything else
The mouse wheel turns: the food on the cutting board while you hold the knife (it was the right click), and what you hold in 45 degree steps before you put it down (the ghost turns with it)
A flip on the griddle is a left click with the spatula now, like every tool. The right click no longer flips
Third person: left click and E act on the nearest thing, right click drops what you hold
Prompts name the button ('Left click · put potato into the pot', 'Right click · put knife here'); the tutorial and the F1 menu show the new controls. Q still puts down, but it is no longer shown
Gamepad: right trigger = left click, left trigger = right click, Y turns
test: Hold a plate and right click on the front counter: does it land where the ghost was? Right click while looking at the floor: does it drop at your feet?
Hold a pan, aim at a pot on the stove and right click: does the pan go next to it, not into it?
Hold the knife over the board with a potato: does the wheel turn the potato, and does dragging down still cut?
Hold the knife over a counter and roll the wheel: does the ghost turn in 45 degree steps, and does the knife lie that way after the right click?
With the spatula, left click a seitan strip on the griddle: does it flip? Does a right click there only put the spatula down (never a flip)?
Play a whole shift with the mouse only: is there anything you still need a key for?

entries.title: Drinks: put the cup under the tap, then fill it
items: Each tap of the drink dispenser has a spot on its drip tray. Take a cup and left click the tap (or the tray under it): the cup snaps under the spout. Right click puts it there too
Hold left click on the tap to fill the cup on its tray: the lever goes down and the drink rises in the cup. Your hands are free while it pours
Left click the lids to put a lid on the filled cup on the tray (or on the one in your hands), then take the cup off the tray with empty hands
Only an empty cup, or an open cup of that tap's drink, fits under a tap. Nobody can take a cup while someone else pours into it
Everyone sees the same pour: the cup on the tray, the lever, the stream and the rising drink
Third person: E puts the cup under the nearest free tap, hold E to pour, E again for the lid, then E takes the cup
The ghost now always shows where a right click would put things down when a left click would not place them (for example next to the pot)
test: Put a cup under the lemonade tap, hold the tap and walk away to do something else halfway: does the cup keep what was poured and the drink stay on the tray?
Fill a cup, lid it on the tray, take it and serve it with an order: does the guest take the drink?
Try to put a lidded cup or a cup of lemonade under the soda tap: is it refused with a reason?
With two players: while one pours, can the other take that cup? (it should say someone is pouring into it)
Overfill a cup: does it spill over the tray and leave the puddle to wipe?

entries.title: Cooking: perfect means best
items: On every station (pan, pot, fryer, griddle, spit) the best stars now come in the Perfect zone of the ring, from the perfect cue to the warning. Good gives a little less, overdone falls off
Names follow the ring: food is called golden, grilled or plain fried / boiled exactly when the ring turns Good. Before that it is pale, lightly fried or half-grilled
Undercooked food no longer passes as the dish: pale fries, half-grilled vegetables or pale seitan in a wrap are only 'close enough'
The pan and the pot cook about twice as fast (a whole potato in the pan is good after about 22 s, in the pot after about 70 s)
For a pan or pot of mixed food, Perfect starts when every part is at its best
test: Shave the spit at the perfect cue: do you get the best stars? Is waiting longer never better?
Lift fries or flip strips at the perfect cue and serve them: the best stars?
Serve fries or a seitan wrap a little early (before the ring turns Good): does the guest say 'close enough'?
Do the pan and the pot feel too fast or too slow now?

entries.title: Feel polish 3
items: Other players now see food fly into the pot, scraps into the trash, the bag into the bin and a plate into the sink, and hear it land, instead of it vanishing from the cook's hand
Other players' put-downs make their tock where the item lands
Station buttons and knobs sink when pressed, for everyone
Sprinting from standing reaches full speed as fast as walking does (about 0.13 s)
Tipping the fryer basket or the griddle onto a plate, and scooping from the spit's tray, show at the click
Third person: both hands on a carried delivery box, and the cloth goes round in the hand while wiping
Eat-in guests put their plate on the dish return after paying instead of walking out with it
The tutorial card sits small in the top right corner and its edge arrow is bigger
The ticket rail hangs higher and tilts towards the kitchen: the guests' order bubbles show under it, and the cards stay bright from below
test: With two players: put food into a pot, scraps into the trash and a plate into the sink while the other watches: does it fly in, with its sound?
Press a stove switch, the fryer's buttons and the spit's knob: do they sink? Does the other player see it?
Sprint from standing: does the start feel snappy now?
Tip the fries basket onto a plate and scoop from the spit tray: does it show at once?
From the kitchen, look at the queue: can you read the order bubbles under the rail, and the rail's cards?

entries.title: Your food corner, and your shop is saved
items: New shop starts a food corner: one dish (fries), walk-up guests who take it to go and pay cash
One goal on screen: save for the rent; the shift summary shows how far you are
The money belongs to the shop: one wallet for the whole crew, every sale and every cost shows for everyone
The supplier drops potatoes at the shelf at the start of each service, paid from the shop wallet; the corner pays a pitch fee after each service
Stations of the restaurant are covered and say so: Opens with your restaurant
The host's game is saved after each service, every 5 minutes, and when you close the shop; Continue on the title screen goes on where you stopped
test: Play a service alone and with a friend: does the shared wallet feel right?
Close the shop, quit, start again: does Continue show the right day and money, and bring you back there?
Is the rent goal too near, too far, or about right?
Does the corner feel like enough to do for one or two cooks?

entries.title: Street-food prices and a menu board
items: Money has cents now: fries $4.00, a wrap about $9.00, a drink $3.00; ingredients cost $0.35 to $1.50
The register's tray has coins of $0.10, $0.20, $0.50, $1 and $2 and notes of $5, $10 and $20; guests pay with $5, $10 or $20 notes
A menu board hangs above the counter: pick a dish and set its price in $0.50 steps
Too dear and fewer guests come and they tip less; cheap brings more guests but less money for each
The food corner's rent goal is $300.00, the pitch fee $5.00 and a new shop starts with $25.00; an older save keeps its progress
test: Do the prices feel like a street-food shop?
Pay a guest in cash: is the change easy to count with the new coins?
Raise the fries by $0.50 for a service, then lower them: do you notice fewer or more guests?
Continue an older save: is your money where you expect it on the way to the rent?
